name: Polycythemia Vera

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in Ashkenazi Jewish populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO 2022 Diagnostic Criteria for Polycythemia Vera

criteria.description: Hemoglobin >16.5 g/dL in men or >16.0 g/dL in women, OR hematocrit >49% in men or >48% in women, OR increased red cell mass
Bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellularity with trilineage growth (panmyelosis) with prominent erythroid, granulocytic, and megakaryocytic proliferation with pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes
Presence of JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All 3 major criteria, OR first 2 major criteria plus the minor criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: JAK2 V617F is found in ~95% of PV cases. JAK2 exon 12 mutations account for most remaining cases. Criterion 2 (bone marrow biopsy) may not be required if hemoglobin is >18.5 g/dL in men or >16.5 g/dL in women with JAK2 mutation and low EPO.

pathognomonic.notes: Intense itching after contact with warm water; highly characteristic of PV

occasional.notes: Burning pain, redness, and warmth of extremities; responds to aspirin
From hyperuricemia due to increased cell turnover

rare.symptomName: Hemorrhage (paradoxical, especially with very high platelet counts)
rare.notes: Acquired von Willebrand disease at very high platelet counts

laboratory: JAK2 V617F mutation positive (~95%) or JAK2 exon 12 mutation
Leukocytosis and thrombocytosis may be present
genetic: JAK2 V617F point mutation in exon 14 (~95% of cases)
Acquired somatic mutation in hematopoietic stem cells
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing panmyelosis with pleomorphic megakaryocytes
Reduced iron stores on marrow biopsy (from increased erythropoiesis)

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated EPO level (vs. low in PV)
Identifiable cause (chronic hypoxia, EPO-producing tumor, smoking)
Different bone marrow morphology (large mature megakaryocytes)
Myelofibrosis shows reticulin/collagen fibrosis on bone marrow biopsy
Leukoerythroblastic blood smear with teardrop cells
Due to dehydration or plasma volume contraction

redFlags: Major thrombotic event (stroke, MI, DVT/PE, Budd-Chiari)
Transformation to myelofibrosis with worsening cytopenias and massive splenomegaly
Severe uncontrolled pruritus significantly impacting quality of life
Paradoxical bleeding with extreme thrombocytosis (acquired von Willebrand)
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016;127(20):2391-2405.
Tefferi A, Barbui T. Polycythemia vera and essential thrombocythemia: 2021 update on diagnosis, risk-stratification and management. Am J Hematol. 2020;95(12):1599-1613.
